goal: Define the Vityo IDE product delivery contract with REQ-001..REQ-009 labels, platform strategy, scope, non-goals, and measurable acceptance targets in Requirements.md.
description: Scope: docs/plan/vityo-product-delivery/Requirements.md only. Context: the existing repository-delivery-convergence plan governs planning-workspace consolidation, not product completion (its Requirements.md non-goals say so explicitly), while the actual product state is partial everywhere except syntax highlighting and shell scaffolding: navigation runs on a token-heuristic StyioSymbolIndex, execution and project-graph adapters await machine payload contracts, packaging has Linux metadata only, and product gates are opt-in; upstream SymPolicy/Vityo already drafted a vityo-product-delivery contract (REQ-001..009, 19 pending checkpoints) that downstream never absorbed. Target: a downstream-owned Requirements.md defining REQ-001 desktop minimal IDE loop (edit/save/compile/run/diagnostics with real execution receipts and machine project-graph payloads), REQ-002 language intelligence truthfulness (compiler-fact navigation/completion with honest capability-gap degradation), REQ-003 runtime visualization event contract, REQ-004 AI provider adapter, REQ-005 theme/profile persistence, REQ-006 module staged lifecycle, REQ-007 platform execution matrix and packaging/distribution, REQ-008 audit and code-health closure (test analyze debt, command-dispatch exhaustiveness, ShellRuntimeModel decomposition, DAP lifecycle, naming/traceability drift), REQ-009 CI and product-gate truthfulness (fail-closed gates, scheduled product matrix); each with users, workflows, and measurable acceptance targets, plus the platform strategy (desktop local-first, Android local-when-CLI-present, iOS cloud-only, Web hosted-only) as a hard constraint set. Design Considerations: adapt upstream REQ taxonomy rather than invent a parallel one, but re-ground every target in downstream evidence since downstream architecture (view_ide/view_render split) is ahead of upstream; keep the convergence plan as the meta-plan and this plan as the product graph. Design Value: gives the 150+ extracted open-work signals a product-level contract to converge on, with stable labels for traceability. Constraints & Risks: must respect Vityo product invariants (Source Buffer authority, staged module updates, iOS cloud-only) from docs/design/Vityo-Product-Spec.md; upstream-blocked items (Styio compiler facts, spio payloads) must be requirements with explicit external dependency statements, not silently dropped.

goal: Record the Vityo module map, layer boundaries, adapter interface contracts, and decomposition plan for oversized modules in Architecture.md.
description: Scope: docs/plan/vityo-product-delivery/Architecture.md only. Context: downstream already enforces a three-layer split (view_ide domain contracts with no Flutter imports, view_render presentation, app composition in app_bootstrap.dart) via scripts/check_architecture_boundaries.py and check_compat_facades.py, but two structural debts remain: shell_runtime_model.dart concentrates ~8900 lines of command dispatch, service lifecycle, and UI state across unrelated product areas, and the adapter seams to Styio (StyioServiceConnector consuming styio-cli-jsonl-v1, optional daemon adapter, DAP process transport) and to spio (ProjectGraphAdapter, ExecutionAdapter with CLI and hosted control-plane routes) each carry capability/blocked semantics that later nodes must implement uniformly. Target: Architecture.md records (1) the module map for both layers with one responsibility per module, (2) the dependency rule UI -> ShellRuntime -> view_ide services -> adapters -> external processes/HTTP with no reverse imports, (3) the interface contracts each implementation node consumes or extends (language service capability routing, execution receipts, project-graph payload source-confidence, module staging states, theme profile store, AI provider adapter), (4) the ShellRuntimeModel decomposition target: per-domain controllers (execution, language, debug, modules, agent, settings) behind the existing ChangeNotifier composition with an explicit target file-size budget, and (5) deliberate pattern decisions with rationale (adapter pattern at all process/HTTP seams, capability-state machine for degradation, staged-update state machine for modules) plus areas that stay pattern-free. Design Considerations: this is a brownfield record aligned with the enforced gates, not a rewrite proposal; number the decomposition steps so the implementation node can land them incrementally with tests green after each. Design Value: keeps ten implementation nodes decoupled and gives the monolith split an agreed target instead of ad-hoc extraction. Constraints & Risks: view_ide must stay Flutter-free (gate-enforced); public contracts under docs/contracts/ are versioned surfaces that adapters must not break silently.

goal: Make app command dispatch total: no code path throws UnimplementedError for any AppCommandId.
description: Scope: command dispatch sites in frontend/vityo_app/lib/src/view_render/shell/shell_runtime_model.dart (~4704-4705 and ~7969) and the command-result contract they return; unit tests per command enum member. Context: unhandled AppCommandId values currently throw UnimplementedError, so a menu entry, palette action, or agent-issued command hitting an unwired branch crashes the shell instead of reporting a capability gap, contradicting the product invariant that unsupported operations surface as explicit blocked states. Constraints & Risks: agent-facing dispatch must stay deterministic (same command, same result shape); this node precedes the monolith decomposition because both edit shell_runtime_model.dart.

goal: Harden external-process lifecycles: DAP adapter shutdown, StyioService daemon restart races, and the terminal PTY decision.
description: Scope: frontend/vityo_app/lib/src/view_ide (debug adapter process transport debug_adapter_process_transport_io.dart ~44-89, StyioService daemon lifecycle owned by the language/execution controllers after decomposition) and view_render/terminal/terminal_surface.dart placeholder paths (~68, ~83, ~280). Context: the DAP transport gives adapters only a 2s grace before kill, risking orphaned lldb-dap/codelldb processes on slow shutdowns; StyioService daemon restart logic can race a kill against an in-flight analysis (scheduler timeouts exist in language_analysis_scheduler.dart ~650-752 but restart interleaving is untested); the interactive terminal still stubs native PTY behavior. Target: DAP shutdown follows terminate-request -> configurable grace -> kill with orphan-PID verification in tests; daemon restart during in-flight analysis yields structured timeout/unavailable results and never hangs or double-spawns; the PTY gap is either implemented for desktop platforms or explicitly declared a capability gap in the capability framework with consistent UX. Design Considerations: lifecycle logic belongs in the owning domain controllers from the decomposition node; use the existing capability-state machine for the PTY decision rather than a bespoke flag; integration tests simulate slow/killed processes. Design Value: process-lifecycle correctness is the difference between an IDE that survives toolchain crashes and one that leaks zombies or hangs; testing it locks the invariant. Constraints & Risks: process tests are timing-sensitive, so use generous simulated delays and deterministic fakes where possible; Windows and POSIX process semantics differ and both are CI targets.

goal: Consume spio machine project-graph payloads with source-confidence labeling replacing inference-only graphs.
description: Scope: frontend/vityo_app/lib/src/view_ide project-graph modules (ProjectGraphAdapter and its io implementation), dependency/workflow lane UI in the owning controller, and project_graph_adapter tests. Context: the project graph currently infers structure from canonical files (pafio.toml, pafio.lock, spio.toml equivalents) because machine payloads (project_graph v1, toolchain_state v1 documented in the spio contracts) were upstream-blocked (Vityo-Implementation-Gaps.md ~92); the adapter already models CLI and hosted control-plane routes. Target: when spio emits project_graph/toolchain_state payloads (CLI or hosted route), the adapter consumes them as the authoritative source with machine-payload confidence; file-inference remains only as the labeled fallback; workflow lanes render dependency, toolchain, and build states from payload fields; tests assert source-confidence transitions between the two modes. Design Considerations: version-check payloads against the documented v1 schemas and fail closed on unknown majors; keep the adapter seam free of UI imports per the layer rule; fixture payloads come from the spio contract examples to avoid contract forking. Design Value: package/workflow surfaces stop guessing and start reflecting the package manager's actual resolution, which is the IDE half of the spio REQ-IDE contract. Constraints & Risks: depends on pafio-nightly publishing payload emission (tracked in its own plan REQ-IDE-001); until then fixtures from contract examples drive the implementation and the external dependency is recorded honestly.

decisions.composition: Machine payloads are authoritative and file inference is a labeled fallback.
decisions.algorithms: Payload major versions are checked before bounded graph decoding.
decisions.data_structures: Project graph snapshots carry nodes, edges, toolchain state, and source confidence.
decisions.state: The latest accepted graph snapshot replaces earlier snapshots atomically.
decisions.isolation: File probing produces fallback facts but never mutates package-manager truth.
decisions.concurrency: Stale graph responses cannot overwrite newer snapshots.

acceptance_criteria.text: Machine payloads are consumed as authoritative with file-inference as labeled fallback, and tests assert the source-confidence transition in both directions.
Unknown payload major versions fail closed with a structured error, covered by a test.

commit.message: project-graph: authoritative machine payloads with labeled inference fallback

goal: Drive runtime visualization from structured execution events instead of raw output scraping.
description: Scope: the runtime visualization surfaces in frontend/vityo_app/lib/src/view_render (runtime panels) and the event decoding in the execution domain controller; no adapter transport changes (receipts land in the execution node). Context: Vityo's product spec positions the IDE as a runtime viewport for stream/resource programs (pulse frames, resource topology, stream state), and the upstream roadmap's REQ-003 defines event-driven visualization; with structured receipts from the execution node, the visualization can subscribe to typed events rather than parsing stdout text. Target: a typed runtime event stream (execution phases, stream pulses, resource reads/writes where the payload provides them) feeding the runtime surface with bounded buffering and backpressure-safe UI updates; text output remains available as the raw console view; golden widget tests cover the event-to-visual mapping. Design Considerations: define the event model in view_ide (Flutter-free) so it is testable headlessly; bound event buffers (drop-oldest with counters) so long runs cannot exhaust memory; do not invent event kinds the toolchain cannot emit yet, and register unsupported kinds as capability gaps. Design Value: differentiates Vityo from a generic editor precisely on Styio's stream/resource semantics while staying honest about payload availability. Constraints & Risks: event vocabulary depends on styio runtime emission maturing; buffer-bound rendering must keep frame budgets within the performance-budget gate.

decisions.composition: Runtime surfaces consume typed events while raw console output remains independently available.
decisions.algorithms: A fixed-capacity ring buffer bounds retained execution events.
decisions.data_structures: Sealed typed events represent phases, pulses, resources, and capability gaps.
decisions.state: Each execution session owns an independently bounded event log.
decisions.isolation: Unknown event kinds become capability gaps and are never guessed.
decisions.concurrency: Event ordering follows the adapter sequence and terminal closure is idempotent.

acceptance_criteria.text: A typed, bounded runtime event stream defined in view_ide feeds the runtime surface, with widget tests covering the event-to-visual mapping.
Unsupported event kinds surface as capability gaps and the performance-budget gate stays green.

goal: Deliver the OpenAI-compatible AI provider adapter with secret-safe configuration and streaming responses.
description: Scope: frontend/vityo_app/lib/src/view_ide agent modules (provider adapter interface and OpenAI-compatible implementation) and the agent panel wiring in view_render; OS secret storage integration flagged in ide_capability_framework.dart TODOs (~241-673). Context: the agent panel exists with capability routing, but the provider seam lacks a production adapter: endpoint/model/key configuration, streamed completion decoding, cancellation, and error taxonomy; API keys must not land in plaintext settings files, and the capability framework already lists OS secret storage as an open TODO. Target: a provider adapter interface in view_ide with an OpenAI-compatible implementation (configurable base URL and model), streaming token delivery with cancellation, structured error states (auth, quota, network, contract), and keys stored via platform secret storage with an explicit non-persistent fallback; the agent panel consumes only the adapter interface. Design Considerations: adapter pattern matches every other external seam in the app; streaming uses the same bounded-buffer discipline as the runtime event stream; never log request bodies or keys (security baseline gate). Design Value: makes the AI surface real for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (local or hosted) without binding the product to one vendor. Constraints & Risks: no network in default CI, so tests run against a local fake server fixture; secret-storage APIs differ per OS and need per-platform test coverage or recorded manual verification.

decisions.algorithms: Streaming decode is incremental and bounded.
decisions.data_structures: Typed chunks and structured provider failures cross the seam.
decisions.state: Credentials remain outside persistent profile state.
decisions.isolation: Network and secret storage stay behind platform adapters.
decisions.concurrency: Cancellation closes one stream exactly once.

acceptance_criteria.text: The OpenAI-compatible adapter streams completions with cancellation and structured error states, proven against a local fake server test.
API keys round-trip through platform secret storage (or the explicit non-persistent fallback) with no plaintext key in settings files or logs, and the security baseline gate passes.

goal: Persist theme and profile customization across sessions through a profile store with import/export.
description: Scope: frontend/vityo_app/lib/src/view_ide settings/theme modules (theme profile store) and the theme editing surface in view_render; settings persistence tests. Context: theme override state exists in memory but the profile store is missing (Vityo-Implementation-Gaps.md ~102-103 and gap-ledger item 9), so customization is lost across sessions; the settings surface already has profile scaffolding and tests reference settings_profile_theme_personalization flows. Target: named theme/profile records persisted through the app's data-store layer, applied at bootstrap, editable through the theme surface, and portable via JSON import/export with schema validation; corrupted profiles fail soft to defaults with a visible notice. Design Considerations: persist through the existing DataStore seam rather than raw file IO in UI code; validate imported profiles against a versioned schema; keep theme tokens semantic (color roles) so future themes stay compatible. Design Value: personalization is retention-level product polish and exercises the persistence seam later nodes (modules) reuse. Constraints & Risks: profile schema growth must stay backward-readable within v1; no plaintext secrets belong in profiles.

goal: Implement the module staged-update lifecycle: download, stage, activate, rollback, and reclaim.
description: Scope: frontend/vityo_app/lib/src/view_ide module_host modules (staging state machine, storage layout, reclaim) and the module management surface in view_render; platform cleanup tests. Context: the product spec mandates staged module updates (a module update never mutates the active copy in place), but staging semantics are UI-only today: real download/staging paths and platform storage reclaim are missing (Vityo-Implementation-Gaps.md ~104-105); the capability framework tracks module hosting as an open area. Target: a staged lifecycle state machine (available -> downloading -> staged -> active -> retired) with atomic activation (rename/pointer swap, never partial overwrite), rollback to the previous active version on failed activation, storage reclaim for retired versions with configurable retention, and integrity verification (digest) before activation; module state survives restarts. Design Considerations: state machine explicitly modeled in view_ide with persisted state; activation atomicity uses the stage-then-swap pattern (mirroring package-manager practice); reclaim never deletes the active version and is covered by platform tests. Design Value: staged lifecycle is a declared product invariant and a data-loss guard, worth the state-machine complexity. Constraints & Risks: module payload sources may be hosted or local; download transport reuses existing adapter seams; interrupted downloads must resume or restart cleanly without corrupting the staging area.

decisions.composition: A persisted state machine coordinates package storage and activation.
decisions.algorithms: Digest verification and stage-then-swap make activation atomic.
decisions.data_structures: Version records track staged, active, retired, and last-known-good packages.
decisions.state: The active pointer changes only after complete validation.
decisions.isolation: Reclaim never touches active or last-known-good versions.
decisions.concurrency: Lifecycle transitions are serialized per module identity.

acceptance_criteria.text: The staged lifecycle state machine implements download/stage/activate/rollback/reclaim with atomic activation and digest verification, covered by state-machine tests.
Module state survives app restart and reclaim never removes the active version (persistence and cleanup tests).

commit.message: modules: staged update lifecycle with atomic activation and reclaim

goal: Make product gates fail closed and give the product matrix a scheduled CI lane so green means proven.
description: Scope: scripts/ecosystem-product-gate.py (~16-26 silent-skip path), scripts/delivery-gate.sh summary reporting, and a scheduled GitHub workflow for the product matrix; documentation of the environment contract in docs/BUILD-AND-DEV-ENV.md. Context: ecosystem-product-gate.py returns exit 0 when the sibling styio-pafio checkout is missing, and the product workflow tests skip without VITYO_PRODUCT_GATE=1, so default green CI proves hygiene and unit floors but not the product loop (CURRENT-STATE.md line 21 admits this); nothing runs the full matrix on a schedule. Target: in CI contexts the product gate fails closed (missing siblings/fixtures = failure, not skip) while local runs may skip with a loud recorded reason in the gate summary; a scheduled workflow provisions sibling checkouts (styio-nightly, pafio-nightly), builds the styio binary, and runs the product matrix with VITYO_PRODUCT_GATE=1, publishing per-REQ evidence artifacts; the delivery-gate summary distinguishes proven/skipped/failed explicitly. Design Considerations: fail-closed-in-CI with explicit local skip keeps developer loops fast while removing false confidence; keep the environment contract (paths, binaries, fixtures) in one documented place consumed by both local and CI runs. Design Value: converts the plan's whole validation story from opt-in to enforced, which REQ-009 exists to guarantee. Constraints & Risks: scheduled cross-repo builds are slower and may flake on upstream breakage; the workflow must pin sibling refs it validated against and record them in the run summary.

goal: Close the platform execution matrix and desktop packaging readiness: installable desktop artifacts and explicit per-platform capability states.
description: Scope: packaging/ (completing packaging/linux required files, adding Windows and macOS packaging definitions), scripts/release-readiness-gate.py extensions, and the per-platform capability declarations in the platform matrix surface; benchmark_results.json relocation out of the app root into release evidence. Context: CI already builds release binaries on Linux/Windows/macOS (local-ci-gate.yml), but only Linux has packaging metadata and it is incomplete (packaging/linux/README.md lists required icons/wrapper/update metadata not all present), no signed installers or update channel exist, mobile strategy is declared (Android local-first, iOS cloud-only) but not surfaced as explicit capability states, and a 1126-line benchmark_results.json sits in frontend/vityo_app as stale committed evidence. Target: release-readiness-gate.py validates a complete per-desktop-OS packaging set (installer definition, icons, desktop/update metadata; signing recorded as configured-or-explicit-gap), the platform matrix surface reports each platform's execution route and capability state truthfully (desktop local, Android local-when-CLI-present, iOS cloud-only, Web hosted-only), and stale benchmark artifacts move to release evidence or CI artifacts. Design Considerations: packaging definitions live per-OS with one responsibility per file; do not fake signing (record it as an explicit gap where certificates are absent); mobile/web packaging is out of scope beyond declaring capability states. Design Value: REQ-007 is the shippability requirement: an IDE that cannot be installed is a demo, and honest platform states prevent overselling mobile support. Constraints & Risks: signing infrastructure may be unavailable in this repo context and must be represented as a recorded gap, not silence; Windows/macOS packaging validation needs those CI runners.

goal: Run the full Validation.md matrix on one head commit and prove REQ-001..REQ-009 with recorded evidence.
description: Scope: execution and evidence recording only; no source changes except fixes the run itself demands routed back to owning nodes. Context: requirements and the validation matrix were defined before implementation; this node proves the same targets end to end instead of trusting per-node snapshots, including the opt-in product matrix that default CI does not cover. Target: on one head commit run the default delivery floor (delivery-gate.sh checkpoint mode, flutter analyze zero-error, full test suite with coverage floors, architecture/facade/security/performance gates, prototype selftest), then the product matrix with sibling checkouts and a built styio binary (sample workflow receipts, language fixture gates, capability matrix verification), then per-REQ grep/UX checks from Validation.md; record pass/fail per REQ label with artifacts, and route failures to owning implementation nodes. Design Considerations: run in the same order as delivery-gate.sh then the scheduled product lane so evidence matches CI semantics; upstream-blocked residuals (compiler facts, spio payloads) are validated on their honest blocked/labeled behavior as Validation.md defines. Design Value: converts eleven node-level claims into one auditable product-delivery proof. Constraints & Risks: requires the documented sibling environment; a red product lane on upstream breakage is a real result to record, not to bypass; this node must not lower any acceptance target defined in Requirements.md.
